column4: REAL outbound-drop (Daniel-caught, watchdog missed). Wedged session 72c50a7c received Daniel's Telegram msgs as proper user turns and generated a text reply to each (2:37pm "Yep, I'm here / Quick status...", 3:01pm "cleared the draft") but NONE were delivered to Telegram - the plugin's outbound text auto-relay had silently died. Daniel got total silence; first delivered reply was 3:52pm from the NEW post-restart session (different text, "Yep, I'm here. What's up?", to re-sent msg #2437). NOT a ghost-text input wedge (C) - inbound turns submitted fine; ghost-text incidental. Watchdog SAW it (no_reply_streak->DEGRADED) but per canary v2 (6/16) treats text-without-send-call as neutral/no-restart, so it neither recovered nor logged - the 6/16 false-POSITIVE fix created a false-NEGATIVE on real relay-death. Also: the daisy-imessage send that started the turn HUNG ~13 min (2:55-3:08pm) on AppleEvent timeout -1712 before failing (unbounded send timeout). Transcript-confirmed + Codex-reviewed.
column5: Manual front-door restart (com.daisy.restart) at 3:06pm restored delivery; confirmed by delivered reply to msg #2437 at 3:52pm. FOLLOW-UPS: (1) canary needs a real Telegram delivery check (not transcript inference) to catch relay-death without re-introducing the 6/15-6/16 false-positive restart loop; (2) bound the daisy-imessage AppleScript send timeout so a failing send fails fast instead of freezing a turn 13 min.

column4: Cause-D outbound relay-death, Daniel-caught (same class as 6/18). Daisy's 03:00 scheduled restart (old bot.pid=55445) brought the session up with the Telegram REPLY TOOL unregistered: every inbound got a proper work-turn and a typed reply in the pane ('Yes - I read it...', 'Yep, I'm here. What do you need?') but NONE reached Telegram. Daniel got silence and kept re-pinging ('confirm you read this', 'Hi you there?'). The watchdog static send_telegram alerts DID reach his phone (separate push path), so the tell was: Daniel sees the robot alerts but not her replies. Watchdog escalated no_reply_streak->DEGRADED but per canary v2 (6/16) does not auto-restart on D, so it neither recovered nor auto-logged. daisy-doctor read HEALTHY first (D is invisible until the streak hits >=3), then flipped DEGRADED; confirmed via pane (reply text, no send call) + Daniel confirming no delivery.
column5: Manual front-door restart (launchctl kickstart com.daisy.restart) ~00:25 PDT; fresh session (new bot.pid=94179) re-registered the reply tool. Confirmed recovered: a NEW inbound got STATUS=OK reason=send_accepted, a delivered reply ('online and ready'), doctor VERDICT HEALTHY. NOTE: right after restart the canary still read DEGRADED on the STALE pre-restart inbound timestamp until the new message landed - not a failed restart; the leftover active outage flag self-clears on the next watchdog tick. 6/18 FOLLOW-UPS: #2 (bound the daisy-imessage send so a bad send fails fast, not a 13-min freeze) SHIPPED today; #1 (canary needs a REAL Telegram delivery check, not transcript inference) STILL OPEN - tonight's relay-death again was not auto-recovered, confirming the gap.

column4: Cause-D relay-death RECURRED (3rd in 3 days, ~08:10, Daniel-caught). Morning: she sent the scheduled message but went silent in Telegram - received inbound + drafted replies in the pane ('Yep, I'm here! Draft's ready above') that never delivered. Ruled OUT poller/zombie (checked both machines: exactly 1 poller chain, no second session, no 409) - outbound reply tool, not a token fight. Root cause confirmed via restart.log: the 03:00 scheduled restart (pid 98959) logged 'OK - poller alive' yet the session came up with the reply MCP tool UNREGISTERED, so the old poller-only healthcheck gave a false OK. Codex-reviewed.
column5: Manual front-door restart restored delivery (send_accepted on a fresh msg, doctor HEALTHY). Integration-tested via real launchctl restart (boot 1 -> reply tool DELIVERED -> OK ~43s). Closes 6/18 FOLLOW-UP #1 (real delivery check, not prose inference).

The reply tool then DIED MID-SESSION: her 5:48 Morning rundown DELIVERED, but the 5:54 photography reply + Yep-8:20 + Here-What-do-you-need (You there? at 6:35) were all TYPED in the pane yet NONE reached Telegram (Daniel screenshot confirms only 5:48 msg arrived). column5: Front-door restart 06:51 (launchctl kickstart com.daisy.restart); boot attempt 1 passed reply-tool healthcheck (DELIVERED 06:52:36, new pid 97627), canary STATUS=OK. column4: CORRECTION + FIX to today's earlier cause-D entry. Deeper investigation reframes the root cause: NOT relay-death and NOT 'reply tool unregistered at boot' (that exact error — No such tool available: ...reply — has occurred exactly ONCE in all transcript history, 05-30, never in the 6/18 or 6/21 windows it was blamed on). Real root cause = REPLY-TOOL ADHERENCE DRIFT: inbound arrives correctly framed (<channel source=plugin:telegram:telegram chat_id=5635145480 ...>), the reply tool works when called, but on conversational turns she answers in PANE TEXT and never calls mcp__plugin_telegram_telegram__reply, so nothing reaches Daniel. Only messages carrying an explicit 'use the reply tool' instruction (scheduled rundown, healthcheck probe) get through — which is why the boot healthcheck passes green while real replies silently die (it FORCES the one tool call real convo skips). Plugin reply instruction is byte-identical pre/post the 6/23 03:07 plugin update (update only touched reaction code); drift happened on both pre- and post-update sessions, so the update is NOT the trigger. Likely historical incidents (6/18, 6/21 x2) were this same drift, mislabeled. Codex concurred across the whole chain.
column5: 3-layer fix shipped today (Codex-reviewed): (1) STOPGAP — injected a standing reply-tool instruction into the live session; she now delivers (Daniel confirmed receipt). (2) DURABLE — added a top-of-file 'Telegram Reply Contract (NON-NEGOTIABLE)' to ~/daisy/CLAUDE.md (backup in patches/); loads on next restart. (3) ENFORCEMENT — new com.daisy.replyguard LaunchAgent (60s) runs guard_reply.py (detects: latest <channel> inbound + substantive pane answer + NO reply call => NEEDS_NUDGE) -> guard_reply.sh debounces 2 ticks, nudges her via lib_send_prompt to resend via the reply tool, escalates ONCE via static send_telegram if the nudge doesn't take. Tested on the frozen photography-drift transcript (NEEDS_NUDGE mid=2565) + dry-run state machine (arm->nudge->escalate->standdown). OPEN FOLLOW-UPS: add an UNFORCED-inbound probe to post_restart_healthcheck.sh (forced probe can't see this class); per-incident re-adjudication of past 'cause D' entries; feature-log entry.
